newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BRAVES PLACE LOFTON ON DISABLED LIST.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BRAVES PLACE LOFTON ON DISABLED LIST.

text.p: The Atlanta Braves were forced to begin a three-game series against the New York Mets on Monday without two of their best players.

The Braves on Monday placed centre fielder Kenny Lofton on the 15-day disabled list with a strained left groin after learning that third baseman Chipper Jones was day-to-day with a slightly sprained left knee.

Lofton, currently sixth in the National League in batting, was injured last Wednesday while running out a single in a 5-3 loss at Toronto. The 30-year-old speedster is hitting .344 in his first season in the NL with three homers, 33 RBI and 19 stolen bases in 67 games.
Jones was injured Sunday in an infield collision at Philadelphia. He was as diognosed as having a slightly sprained knee with no structural damage.
That came as a huge relief as Jones missed the entire 1994 season with a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee.

Jones went 4-for-5 with a home run and three RBI in Atlanta's 12-5 win over the Phillies Sunday, but he had to be helped off the field after colliding with first baseman Mike Mordecai while running under an infield popup in the eighth inning.
The switch-hitting Jones batted .309 with 30 homers and a team-leading 110 RBI last season. He is hitting .295 with 10 homers and 53 RBI this year.
To fill his Lofton's roster spot, the Braves recalled outfielder Danny Bautista from Triple-A Richmond, where he was batting .282 with two homers and 28 RBI in 46 games.
